title: Without You All Is Darkness
desc: Without You All Is Darkness is a 1956 West German drama film directed by and starring Curd Jürgens. Eva Bartok, René Deltgen and Ursula Grabley also star.

title: 1054 Forsytia
desc: 1054 Forsytia is a dark background asteroid, approximately 46 kilometers in diameter, from the outer regions of the asteroid belt. It was discovered on 20 November 1925, by astronomer Karl Reinmuth at the Heidelberg-Königstuhl State Observatory in southwest Germany and assigned provisional designation 1925 WD. title: Howard Engel
desc: Howard Engel CM was a Canadian mystery author and CBC producer who resided in Toronto, Ontario. He was famous for his Benny Cooperman detective series, set in the Niagara Region in and around the city of Grantham, Ontario, mirroring St. Catharines, Ontario, where he was born. He was one of the founding authors of Crime Writers of Canada in 1982.

title: Louis, Duke of Montpensier
desc: Louis, Duc de Montpensier was the second Duke of Montpensier, a French Prince of the Blood, military commander and governor. He began his military career during the Italian Wars, and in 1557 was captured after the disastrous battle of Saint-Quentin. title: Peacock in the Park
desc: Peacock in the Park is an annual LGBTQ variety show, held at Washington Park in Portland, Oregon, in the United States. The event was founded in 1987 and ran for 18 years, until it was replaced by the Peacock After Dark event in 2005. Due to popular demand, Peacock in the Park returned in 2014. title: Mass Effect Galaxy
desc: Mass Effect Galaxy was a mobile game for iOS developed by BioWare and published by Microsoft Game Studios. title: Track of the Zombie
desc: Track of the Zombie is the 71st title of the Hardy Boys series of mystery books for children and teens, written by Franklin W. Dixon. It was published by Wanderer Books in 1982.

title: Plants in space
desc: The growth of plants in outer space has elicited much scientific interest moving from fictional discussion such as the trees on the brick moon space station in the 1869 short story "The Brick Moon". title: Alotus
desc: Alotus is the thirteenth album by the Finnish experimental rock band Circle.

title: Persephone
desc: In ancient Greek mythology and religion, Persephone is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter. She became the queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, the king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage. title: Shiver (novel)
desc: Shiver is a 2021 British mystery thriller and the debut novel of Allie Reynolds, a former freestyle snowboarder. Published in the United Kingdom through Headline, the novel shifts between the past and present to tell the story of arguments and rivalries between competitive snowboarders that may have led to murder.

title: Secretary of Agriculture (Philippines)
desc: The Secretary of Agriculture is a member of the Cabinet of the Philippines in charge of the Department of Agriculture.

title: Alex Karczmar
desc: Alexander George Karczmar was a Polish-American neuroscientist and academic. He was professor and chairman of the Department of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics at Loyola University Medical Center from 1956 to 1986, and director of its Institute for Mind, Drugs, and Behavior.

title: Moonraker (novel)
desc: Moonraker is the third novel by the British author Ian Fleming to feature his fictional British Secret Service agent James Bond. It was published by Jonathan Cape on 5 April 1955 and featured a cover design conceived by Fleming. The plot is derived from a Fleming screenplay that was too short for a full novel, so he added the passage of the bridge game between Bond and the industrialist Hugo Drax.

title: 88 Aquarii
desc: 88 Aquarii, officially named Safina, is a star in the equatorial constellation of Aquarius. 88 Aquarii is the Flamsteed designation, though it also bears the Bayer designation c2 Aquarii. In dark conditions it is visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude of +3.68. Based upon parallax measurements, this star is at a distance of around 271 light-years from Earth.

title: Council of Ministers (Italy)
desc: The Council of Ministers is the principal executive organ of the Government of Italy. It comprises the President of the Council, all the ministers, and the Undersecretary to the Prime Minister. Deputy ministers and junior ministers are part of the government, but are not members of the Council of Ministers.

title: Tamjanika
desc: Tamjanika, Temjanika or Tamyanka is a grape variety from the muscat family, grown in Serbia, North Macedonia and Bulgaria. It is named after tamjan ("frankincense"), due to the intense scent from the ripe grapes, which can be detected several metres away. The berries are small, very dark purple, almost perfect spheres. They ripen in mid September.

title: Z.Vex Fuzz Factory
desc: The Fuzz Factory is a fuzz pedal manufactured by Z.Vex Effects and first released in 1995. At its core, the Fuzz Factory uses a circuit similar to a modified Fuzz Face, but includes unique controls to alter the biasing of its germanium transistors, relying on their instability when incorrectly biased to give users the ability to create a variety of unconventional sounds alongside traditional fuzz

title: Harkhebi
desc: Harkhebi was an ancient Egyptian astronomer who lived in Ptolemaic Egypt during the rule of the Ptolemaic dynasty. He was known as the priest of Selket. He specialized in the treatment of snake bites and scorpion stings. He also kept record of day and night, tracking the rising and setting of the sun. This is how it was deduced in 1872 that he was present in the temple of Illahun.

title: Ishmael Butler
desc: Ishmael Reginald Butler is an American rapper, songwriter and record producer. As Butterfly, he is a founding member of the hip-hop trio Digable Planets; as Palaceer Lazaro, he is the founder and principal creative figure behind the experimental hip-hop project Shabazz Palaces. title: Qahedjet
desc: Qahedjet could be the Horus name of an ancient Egyptian king (pharaoh), who may have ruled during the 3rd Dynasty or could be a voluntarily archaistic representation of Thutmose III. title: The House That Jack Built (1900 film)
desc: The House That Jack Built is a 1900 British short, silent trick film directed by George Albert Smith featuring a boy who knocks over a house made of bricks built by his sister and then rebuilds it when the original sequence is shown in reverse. title: Druggability
desc: Druggability is a term used in drug discovery to describe a biological target that is known or predicted to bind with high affinity to a drug. Importantly, binding of the drug to the target must result in a functional change that provides a therapeutic benefit to the patient. In other words, the target must be disease-modifying. title: Jean Baptiste Joseph Delambre
desc: Jean Baptiste Joseph, chevalier Delambre was a French mathematician, astronomer, historian of astronomy, and geodesist. He was also director of the Paris Observatory, and author of well-known books on the history of astronomy from ancient times to the 18th century. He is known for his expedition to gather geodetical measurements in order to define the metre.

title: The Idiots (1998 film)
desc: The Idiots is a 1998 black comedy drama film written and directed by Lars von Trier. It is his first film made in compliance with the Dogme 95 Manifesto, and is also known as Dogme #2. It is the second film in Trier's “Golden Heart” trilogy, preceded by Breaking the Waves (1996) and succeeded by Dancer in the Dark (2000). It is among the first films to be shot entirely with digital cameras.
